name: Ottoman Seizure of Gallipoli
summary: An earthquake destroys the walls of Gallipoli in March 1354; Ottoman prince Suleyman immediately occupies the abandoned fortress, giving the Ottomans their first permanent foothold in Europe. Byzantine Emperor John V Palaiologos demands evacuation but lacks the military force to compel it. The Ottomans use Gallipoli as a staging point to flood soldiers across the Hellespont, beginning the conquest of Thrace. Within a decade, Adrianople falls (1369), surrounding Constantinople on the European side.

_quarry.structural_significance: The defining moment of Ottoman expansion into Europe; control of Gallipoli means control of the Hellespont crossing; Constantinople is now strategically surrounded; the Ottomans never again need to fight for a European bridgehead; from Gallipoli flow the conquests of Thrace, Bulgaria, Serbia, Greece, and ultimately Constantinople itself
